e-5904.knowledge_point: Computing the Complex Eigenvalues of a Matrix
e-5904.problem: Compute the eigenvalues of the matrix $[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
e-5904.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\, A-\lambda I \mathbin{:}$

﻿﻿﻿

$$
[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we compute the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-2(-2) & =0 \\ 1-2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-2)\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4(1)(5)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{-16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 4\text{i}}{2} \\  & =1\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda=1\pm 2\textrm{i}.$

after.problem: Compute the eigenvalues of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -17 & -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 1 \\ -17 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we compute the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 1 \\ -17 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-1(-17) & =0 \\ -1-\lambda +\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+17 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-16 \\ \lambda  & =\pm 4\text{i}\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Compute the eigenvalues of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we compute the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-1(-2) & =0 \\ 4-4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +6 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-4)\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4(1)(6)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{-8}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 2\sqrt{2}\text{i}}{2} \\  & =2\pm \sqrt{2}\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =2\pm \sqrt{2}\text{i}.$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Complex Eigenvalues of a Matrix
content.problem: Compute the eigenvalues of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we compute the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-1(-2) & =0 \\ 4-4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +6 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-4)\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4(1)(6)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{-8}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 2\sqrt{2}\text{i}}{2} \\  & =2\pm \sqrt{2}\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =2\pm \sqrt{2}\text{i}.$
